function: DQN allocates time slots to beam snapshots in a beam-hopping LEO downlink to minimize total power under traffic demands; power allocation is analytic, not learned (pp. 3-4).
system: Downlink LEO satellite at 600 km, 16 fixed beams, 4 active, 2-6 FDMA users per beam, 2 GHz carrier, 10 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (pp. 2, 4).
method: Deep Q-network (two hidden layers of 512 neurons, sigmoid), epsilon-greedy, replay buffer, target network, log-cosh loss, Adam; reinforcement learning on episodes of channel instances (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Own model: free-space path loss at 2 GHz, 4 dB log-normal shadowing, Bessel beam pattern, 1000 user-deployment instances x 9 elevation angles (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Training and evaluation use separate sets of 1000 x 9 episodes; evaluation sweeps total users 32-96 and traffic demand 10-50 Mbps; training configuration not stated (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: per-slot optimization [5], iterative optimization [6]. Learned: DNN-based time-slot allocation [8] with the paper's power allocation (pp. 4-5).
metrics: Capacity-demand gap, total power consumption, cost function value over episodes, computational time (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Measured computation time versus users (Fig. 7): proposed DQN below 10^4 ms, per-slot and iterative about 10^6 ms (read from plot); no order or FLOPs (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 2: "that depends on the shadowing effect and free-space path loss at the carrier frequency". The channel is a custom model (log-normal shadowing, free-space loss, Bessel beam pattern); no 3GPP TR 38.811 model, public ray-tracing dataset, or measured data is cited.
q2_support: p. 4: "ensuring independence from the evaluation dataset". Training and evaluation use separate episodes of the same kind (user deployments, 9 elevation angles); no model trained on one number of users, traffic level or configuration is stated to be tested on another.
q3_support: p. 4: "This is an iterative method for optimizing time slot and transmit power" (non-learned [6], also per-slot [5]) and p. 4: "This is a DNN-based time slot allocation approach, introduced in [8]" (earlier learned method); all compared on CDG and total power in Figs. 3, 5 and 6.
q4_support: p. 5: "we evaluate the execution time of each scheme as the number of users increases". Fig. 7 plots the measured computational time of the proposed DQN against the per-slot, iterative and DNN-based schemes.
q5_support: p. 4: "each data instance represents a change in user deployment". The data are generated by the authors' own simulation; no code or data link, DOI, or public dataset is given anywhere in the letter.
notes: Included: letter with a DQN for beam-hopping time-slot allocation in a LEO link, results on pp. 4-5. Area 6 (resource and beam control for satellite links); the satellite rule of step 1 keeps learned resource allocation and beams in the physical layer although the title says scheduling. Power allocation is the analytic matrix inversion of [6] (p. 4), only the time-slot allocation is learned. The only mention of pre-training over many configurations (p. 4) is a suggested mitigation, so q2 is 0. Table I lists traffic demand 15-35 Mbps while the Fig. 6 axis spans 10-50 Mbps. Table I and Figs. 4-7 read as page images. Title on p. 1 matches; DOI printed on p. 1 matches.
